AWS Graviton4-based R8g instances offer larger instance sizes with up to 3x more vCPU (up to 48xlarge) and memory (up to 1.5TB) than Graviton3-based R7g instances. These instances are up to 30% faster for web applications, 40% faster for databases, and 45% faster for large Java applications compared to AWS Graviton3-based R7g instances. R8g instances are available in 12 different instance sizes, including two bare metal sizes. They offer up to 50 Gbps enhanced networking bandwidth and up to 40 Gbps of bandwidth to the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). To learn more, see Amazon EC2 R8g Instances . To explore how to migrate your workloads to Graviton-based instances, see AWS Graviton Fast Start program and Porting Advisor for Graviton . To get started, see the AWS Management Console .

title: Amazon EC2 R8gd instances are now available in additional regions
announcement_text: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) R8gd instances are available in AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) region. These instances feature up to 11.4 TB of local NVMe-based SSD block-level storage and are powered by AWS Graviton4 processors, delivering up to 30% better performance over Graviton3-based instances. These instances are built on the AWS Nitro System and are a great fit for applications that need access to high-speed, low latency local storage. R8gd instances are available in 12 different sizes. They provide up to 50 Gbps of network bandwidth and up to 40 Gbps of bandwidth to the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). Additionally, customers can now adjust the network and Amazon EBS bandwidth on these instances by 25% using EC2 instance bandwidth weighting conﬁguration, providing greater ﬂexibility with the allocation of bandwidth resources to better optimize workloads. These instances offer Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking on 24xlarge, 48xlarge, metal-24xl, and metal-48xl sizes. To learn more, see R8gd instances . To explore how to migrate your workloads to Graviton-based instances, see AWS Graviton Fast Start program . To get started, see the AWS Management Console .

title: Amazon Quick now supports brand templates for on-brand presentations and documents
announcement_text: Starting today, you can upload brand templates in Amazon Quick, allowing you to create presentations and documents that match your approved visual identity. Brand managers set up a template once and everyone gets on-brand output, without hunting for the right file in each chat. Brand managers upload PowerPoint or Word templates, or pull them from a connected file store such as SharePoint. Quick extracts the colors, fonts, logos, layouts and brand rules from each file. A brand manager reviews and edits what Quick found before publishing it to the whole organization. Quick also follows a template's rules as it creates new assets. If a request breaks a rule, Quick explains why and suggests an on-brand alternative. For each task, Quick picks the best-fit template based on guidance the brand manager writes. Users can still choose a different template. Administrators decide who can create and publish brand templates using custom permissions, ensuring that only the proper members of brand, marketing, or other approved teams can set visual standards. Brand assets are generally available today in the Amazon Quick desktop app. To learn more, see the Amazon Quick documentation, or create an account for free and start using Quick in minutes.

title: AWS Lambda supports OAuth authentication for self-managed Apache Kafka event sources
announcement_text: AWS Lambda now supports OAuth authentication for self-managed Apache Kafka event source mappings (ESM), including Kafka clusters that customers run themselves and managed offerings such as Confluent Cloud, Aiven, and Redpanda. With this launch, customers can authenticate their Lambda Kafka consumers through their enterprise identity provider, helping them meet the security and compliance requirements for their Kafka applications. Customers building event-driven Kafka workloads for use cases such as payment processing, fraud detection, and real-time data pipelines use Kafka ESM to build serverless Kafka consumers. Kafka ESM provides automatic scaling, error handling, batching, and event filtering. Previously, Kafka ESM supported only SASL/PLAIN, SASL/SCRAM, and mutual TLS (mTLS) as authentication methods , so customers in regulated industries that require OAuth could not use Kafka ESM with their clusters. With OAuth support, customers can use their enterprise identity provider, such as Amazon Cognito or Okta, to authenticate their Kafka ESM and apply the same identity governance and access policies across their Kafka clusters and Lambda consumers. This capability is available in all AWS commercial Regions where self-managed Kafka ESM is available. To use OAuth authentication, create a new Kafka ESM with your authentication configuration through the AWS Management Console, Lambda API, AWS CLI, AWS CloudFormation, or AWS SAM. To learn more, see the AWS Lambda developer guide and AWS Lambda pricing .

title: Amazon EC2 C8gd and M8gd instances are now available in additional regions
announcement_text: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) C8gd and M8gd instances with up to 11.4 TB of local NVMe-based SSD block-level storage are now available in additional regions. C8gd instances are now available in Europe (Stockholm), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), and Asia Pacific (Seoul). M8gd instances are now available in Europe (Stockholm), US West (N. California), and Asia Pacific (Singapore). These instances are powered by AWS Graviton4 processors, delivering up to 30% better performance over Graviton3-based instances. They have up to 40% higher performance for I/O intensive database workloads, and up to 20% faster query results for I/O intensive real-time data analytics than comparable AWS Graviton3-based instances. These instances are built on the AWS Nitro System and are a great fit for applications that need access to high-speed, low latency local storage. Each instance is available in 12 different sizes. They provide up to 50 Gbps of network bandwidth and up to 40 Gbps of bandwidth to the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). Additionally, customers can now adjust the network and Amazon EBS bandwidth on these instances by 25% using EC2 instance bandwidth weighting configuration, providing greater flexibility with the allocation of bandwidth resources to better optimize workloads. These instances offer Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking on 24xlarge, 48xlarge, metal-24xl, and metal-48xl sizes. C8gd instances are ideal for compute-intensive workloads such as high-performance web servers, batch processing, distributed analytics, ad serving, video encoding, and gaming servers. M8gd instances are well-suited for balanced workloads including application servers, microservices, enterprise applications, and small to medium databases. To learn more, see Amazon C8gd Instances and Amazon M8gd Instances . To explore how to migrate your workloads to Graviton-based instances, see AWS Graviton Fast Start program and Porting Advisor for Graviton . To get started, see the AWS Management Console .

title: Amazon EC2 C9g, C9gd, M9g, and M9gd instances are now available in additional regions
announcement_text: Starting today, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) C9g and C9gd instances are available in the Asia Pacific (Malaysia, Seoul, Singapore) regions. Amazon EC2 M9g and M9gd instances are available in the Asia Pacific (Malaysia) and Europe (Spain) regions. These instances are powered by AWS Graviton5 processors, the fifth generation of custom-designed CPUs, which deliver the best price performance for a broad range of workloads running on Amazon EC2. C9g and C9gd instances and M9g and M9gd instances deliver up to 25% better compute performance than AWS Graviton4-based C8g, C8gd, M8g, and M8gd instances. They are up to 30% faster for databases, up to 35% faster for web applications, and up to 35% faster for machine learning. These instances are built on the sixth-generation AWS Nitro System and are the first to feature the Nitro Isolation Engine . The Isolation Engine uses formal verification to provide mathematical assurance that customer workloads are isolated from each other and from AWS operators, pioneering a new standard for mathematically proven cloud security. C9g instances are ideal for compute-intensive workloads such as high-performance computing (HPC), batch processing, gaming, video encoding, scientific modeling, distributed analytics, CPU-based machine learning (ML) inference, real-time analytics, and ad serving. M9g instances serve a broad range of general-purpose workloads, including application servers, microservices, gaming, caching, and containers. They also deliver the performance needed for agentic AI use cases like real-time reasoning, code generation, and multi-step orchestration. C9gd and M9gd instances add local NVMe-based SSD block-level storage for workloads that need high-speed, low-latency local storage for scratch space, temporary files, and caches. C9g, C9gd, M9g, and M9gd instances are available for purchase in these regions via Savings Plans, On-Demand, Spot Instances, Dedicated Instances, or Dedicated Hosts. Level up your compute with AWS Graviton and get started today with C9g and M9g .

title: Amazon EC2 M8id instances now available in Asia Pacific (Malaysia) and Asia Pacific (Sydney)
announcement_text: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) M8id instances with up to 22.8 TB of local NVMe-based SSD block-level storage are now available in Asia Pacific (Malaysia) and Asia Pacific (Sydney). M8id instances are designed for workloads that require a balance of compute and memory resources along with high-speed, low-latency local block storage, including data logging, media processing, and medium-sized data stores. Amazon EC2 M8id instances offer 3 times more vCPUs, memory and local storage compared to previous sixth-generation instances. These instances deliver up to 43% higher compute performance and 3.3 times more memory bandwidth compared to previous sixth-generation M6id instances. They also deliver up to 46% higher performance for I/O intensive database workloads, and up to 30% faster query results for I/O intensive real-time data analytics compared to previous sixth generation instances. Additionally, customers can now adjust the network and Amazon EBS bandwidth on these instances by 25% using EC2 instance bandwidth weighting configuration, providing greater flexibility with the allocation of bandwidth resources to better optimize workloads. These instances offer Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking on 24xlarge, 48xlarge, metal-24xl, and metal-48xl sizes. Customers can purchase these instances via Savings Plans, On-Demand instances, and Spot instances. For more information visit the Amazon EC2 M8id page.

title: Amazon S3 Vectors metadata pre-filtering is now available in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions
announcement_text: Amazon S3 Vectors metadata pre-filtering is now available in the AWS GovCloud (US-East) and AWS GovCloud (US-West) Regions. Pre-filtering evaluates metadata filters before running similarity search, returning up to 5x more of the matching vectors when your filter is selective. S3 Vectors also adds a prefix match operator ($startsWith) for filtering on values like paths and URLs. Together, these improvements give your retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic, and semantic-search applications more complete results when you filter, so your applications return more relevant answers. S3 Vectors provides native support to store and query vectors in Amazon S3, delivering purpose-built, cost-optimized vector storage and query at billion-vector scale. With this launch, indexes in new vector buckets in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions use metadata pre-filtering by default, with no change to how you write vectors with PutVectors or run filtered queries with QueryVectors. To use pre-filtering on an existing index, update it in place with the UpdateIndexMode API. You can also compare pre-filtering against your current filtering on the same index, using a per-query parameter on QueryVectors, before you update. Metadata pre-filtering is available at no additional cost in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon S3 Vectors is available, and in the AWS China Regions. We are in the process of deploying this change and plan to complete the deployment in the coming days. To get started, use the AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or the Amazon S3 console. To learn more, visit the Amazon S3 Vectors documentation and the AWS News blog .

title: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom Tooling blueprints
announcement_text: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio now supports custom Tooling blueprints, giving domain administrators the ability to define the foundation of every project by using their own AWS CloudFormation templates. Administrators can tailor project environments to meet organization-specific requirements, such as IAM role names that comply with company naming standards or custom permissions boundaries instead of AWS managed policies. Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio administrators start by authoring a CloudFormation template that describes the project environment they need, then register it as a custom Tooling blueprint. The service validates the template at registration and again after each project deployment, confirming that the required resources exist before any team member uses the project. Templates can include any CloudFormation-supported resource, such as AWS Lake Formation grants, Amazon Athena workgroups, or VPC security groups, and work across multiple AWS accounts and Regions without per-project edits. At deployment time, the service automatically populates reserved template parameters, such as the project ID and domain ID, so administrators define the template once and apply it everywhere. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio is available. To learn more, visit the Custom blueprints as Tooling documentation .

title: AWS Security Hub now exports findings to S3 in CSV or JSON format
product_change_reason: Security Hub exports findings directly to S3
announcement_text: Today, AWS Security Hub announces support for exporting findings to Amazon S3 in CSV or JSON (OCSF) format. Security teams that need findings outside the console for use cases such as compliance reporting and audit evidence can now export findings from every findings page in the Security Hub console, including Threats, Exposure, Vulnerabilities, Posture Management, Sensitive Data, and All Findings, without building and maintaining their own extraction pipelines. With this launch, you can start an export on demand from the findings page you are viewing and have Security Hub deliver the results to an S3 bucket in your account. You can choose CSV when you want to review or share findings in a spreadsheet or export in JSON if you need these findings in Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) format. Findings export is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Security Hub is available. To learn more, visit the AWS Security Hub User Guide at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-v2-findings-export.html .

title: TwelveLabs Pegasus 1.5 model now available on Amazon Bedrock
announcement_text: Amazon Bedrock now supports TwelveLabs Pegasus 1.5, a video-to-text model that generates structured, time-coded metadata from video. Until now, finding a moment in a large video library meant knowing where to look before you could ask about it. Pegasus 1.5 reads an entire video and labels what happens and when, turning footage into data your applications can query. You define what matters to your business, such as editorial segments, speaker changes, sports plays, or brand appearances, and Pegasus 1.5 finds those moments across the video and returns them with timestamps. It analyzes what it sees, hears, and reads on screen in a single pass, with no pre-indexing or ingestion pipeline to build first. Pegasus 1.5 is accessible through the US and Global cross-Region inference profiles. To get started, visit the Amazon Bedrock product page, access the model in the Amazon Bedrock console, or see the Amazon Bedrock documentation for supported Regions, APIs, features, and pricing.

title: AWS now lets customers sign up for AWS and pay invoices using ACH direct debit
product_change_reason: Adds ACH debit signup and payment method.
announcement_text: Starting today, AWS customers in the United States can use a US bank account to sign up for AWS and pay for their AWS services through ACH direct debit. This feature provides a convenient and secure way to manage AWS payments directly from a USD bank account. Customers can securely connect a personal or business US bank account and use it to pay AWS invoices. Previously, new AWS customers needed a credit or debit card to complete signing up for an account. During sign-up, customers can choose Bank Account on the AWS sign-up page, select their bank, and authenticate using their bank's mobile app or online banking credentials. This securely verifies ownership and links their bank account to their AWS account. By default, the account will be used to pay future AWS invoices. Existing customers can add a bank account from the Payment preferences page in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console. They choose Add payment method, select Link your bank account, and follow the same bank-selection and authentication flow. Once verified, the bank account is available as a payment method to pay future AWS invoices.. ACH direct debit is available at no additional cost to AWS customers for USD bank accounts. To learn more, see Managing ACH direct debit .

title: Announcing consumption-based pricing for short-term memory in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
product_change_reason: Replaces per-event charges with consumption-based ingestion, retrieval and storage rates; the post describes no new memory operation or TTL functionality.
product_change_basis: Source adjudication; primary-reader commercial-tail source review
announcement_text: Announcing consumption-based pricing for short-term memory in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory now prices short-term memory (STM) based on the data your agents ingest, retrieve, and store, replacing the previous flat rate per event. AgentCore memory gives agents in-session context through short-term memory and persistent knowledge across sessions through long-term memory. With consumption-based pricing, developers building agents that write frequent, small events pay in proportion to what they use. STM is priced across three dimensions: ingestion at $1.00 per GB, retrieval at $0.20 per GB, and storage at $0.10 per GB-month. Ingestion and retrieval are billed per event with a 12 KB minimum and 64 KB maximum billable size, while storage is billed on each event's actual size. Most workloads see lower costs, with small-payload use cases seeing the largest reductions. You can manage storage costs by setting a shorter time to live (TTL) on your memory resources. Long-term memory pricing is unchanged. Consumption-based pricing for AgentCore Memory short-term memory is available in all AWS Regions where AgentCore Memory is offered. To get started, visit the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore pricing page .

title: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey introduces ElastiCache Insights
announcement_text: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey now features ElastiCache Insights, a pre-built dashboard in Amazon CloudWatch for your node-based clusters. ElastiCache Insights brings cluster health, memory, compute, network, command throughput, latency, keyspace, and errors into a single view sourced from a set of OpenTelemetry metrics that ElastiCache publishes automatically. You can use ElastiCache Insights to check the health of your cache workloads across a Region at a glance, detect when a node nears its memory, network, or connection limits, and filter your view to a cluster, shard, node, or Availability Zone. You can also save a copy as the starting point for a custom dashboard tailored to your workload. With detailed monitoring, you can choose metrics to publish every 15 seconds and view them on the Metrics tab or in your custom dashboard. CloudWatch pricing for OpenTelemetry metrics applies to ElastiCache detailed monitoring. To get started, open the Metrics tab for a cluster in the Amazon ElastiCache console and choose View in ElastiCache Insights. You can also choose ElastiCache Insights under Infrastructure Monitoring in the Amazon CloudWatch console. ElastiCache Insights is available for node-based Valkey clusters in all AWS Regions where Amazon CloudWatch supports OpenTelemetry metrics. To learn more about ElastiCache Insights, see Monitoring ElastiCache with OpenTelemetry metrics in the Amazon ElastiCache User Guide.

title: Amazon EMR now supports native data quality checks in Apache Spark jobs
announcement_text: Amazon EMR now validates data quality natively within Apache Spark jobs. Data engineering teams can catch quality issues inline before bad data reaches downstream systems, without building or maintaining separate validation infrastructure. Amazon EMR Data Quality, powered by AWS Glue, is available at no additional cost and uses the same declarative rules language (Data Quality Definition Language) and APIs as AWS Glue for a consistent experience across both engines, and works with Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi, and Delta Lake across EC2, EKS, and Serverless deployment modes. With this feature, you can author validation rules in your Spark scripts or reference rules stored in the AWS Glue Data Catalog, and then apply them at any stage of your pipeline i.e., after reading data, during transformation, or after processing. With 30+ rule types, including dynamic rules that compare against historical runs and ML-based anomaly detection for tracking drift over time without specifying fixed thresholds, Amazon EMR Data Quality provides the flexibility of choosing the validation framework that fits your needs. You can take actions like failing a pipeline, filtering invalid records, or routing them to quarantine based on the quality evaluation results. Results are produced at the dataset, rule, and row level, so that you can easily identify which records or rules are driving the quality failures. Amazon EMR Data Quality is available on AWS runtime for Apache Spark (emr-spark-8.1.0) in all AWS Commercial, AWS GovCloud (US), and AWS China Regions. To get started, visit Amazon EMR Data Quality documentation and add DQDL rules for data quality validation to the Spark scripts of your EMR workloads.

title: Amazon EC2 G7 instances now available in Europe (Frankfurt) and Europe (Stockholm) Regions
announcement_text: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) G7 instances powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs are now available in Europe (Frankfurt) and Europe (Stockholm) Regions. G7 instances deliver up to 4.6x AI inference performance and up to 2.1 graphics performance compared to G6 instances. G7 instances also deliver faster performance for GPU-accelerated data analytics workloads. Customers can use G7 instances for deploying AI models for language translation, video and image analysis, speech recognition and recommender systems. They also accelerate graphics workloads such as creating and rendering real-time, cinematic-quality graphics and game streaming. Additionally, G7 instances support video transcoding, spatial computing, and data analytics workloads. G7 instances feature up to 8 NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs with 32 GB of memory per GPU and custom Intel Xeon 6 processors. They support up to 192 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) and up to 700 Gbps of Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking bandwidth. They also support up to 768 GiB of system memory, and up to 7.6 TB of local NVMe SSD storage. You can use G7 instances for Amazon EC2 in the following AWS Regions: US West (Oregon), US East (N. Virginia, Ohio) and Europe (Spain, Frankfurt, Stockholm). You can purchase G7 instances as On-Demand Instances, Spot Instances, or as part of Savings Plans. To get started, visit the AWS Management Console , AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), and AWS SDKs. To learn more, visit the G7 instance page .

title: AWS Lambda announces Lambda Web Functions
product_change_reason: Lambda Web Functions introduces direct HTTP-server programming with concurrent requests active-CPU billing and multi-region routing, matching the agreed anchor.
product_change_basis: Source adjudication; cross-reader high-level audit by batch1 reader
announcement_text: AWS Lambda announces Lambda Web Functions, a new serverless compute primitive where your code handles HTTP requests directly. Your code listens on a port and handles requests as it would on any HTTP server. You use frameworks you already know, such as Express or Hono, with no adapters or custom configuration. This enables you to serve workloads such as AI inference endpoints, server-side rendered (SSR) web apps, streaming API endpoints, microservices, and webhooks. You pay for active CPU time and the memory your environment holds, not for idle CPU time your code spends waiting on databases or downstream services. With this launch, we are also renaming existing Lambda functions to Lambda Event Functions, a naming change only that requires no code changes or redeployments for your existing functions. Builders use Lambda to go from code to production quickly and without managing servers, across event-driven pipelines, request-response APIs, and data processing. As AI-driven development accelerates, they want to build locally and deploy with a familiar programming model and pay for workloads based on active CPU usage, while serving users with low latency. Lambda Web Functions delivers this. Today, Lambda Web Functions supports the Node.js runtime. A single warm execution environment can serve multiple concurrent requests, which reduces cold starts by orders of magnitude. You can stream results to clients incrementally with native HTTP streaming. You can create and configure Lambda Web Functions using the AWS Lambda API, Agent Toolkit for AWS , AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, AWS CloudFormation, AWS SAM, AWS CDK, or the AWS SDKs. With multi-Region routing, you can deploy once and serve each request from the Region closest to the end user. Web Functions support Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) connectivity, allowing your function to access resources that exist within a VPC. Lambda Web Functions is available today in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Ireland). For the current list, see the AWS Capabilities by Region page. To learn more, see the Lambda Web Functions developer guide . For pricing details, see AWS Lambda Pricing . To see Lambda Web Functions in action, see the AWS News Blog announcement .

title: Amazon CloudFront now supports AWS Lambda Web Functions as an origin
product_change_reason: CloudFront supports Lambda Web Function origins
announcement_text: Starting today, you can deliver web applications built on AWS Lambda Web Functions through CloudFront's global edge network. With CloudFront in front of a Lambda Web Function, you get TLS termination at the edge for lower latency and faster connections, caching for better performance, and custom domains with managed TLS certificates. No changes to application code are needed. CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC) restricts your Lambda Web Function so it's reachable only through CloudFront, so unintended requests that bypass your security protections do not reach your origin. With OAC in place, CloudFront's edge network protects your Lambda Web Function from network-layer DDoS attacks, and you can attach AWS WAF for additional application-layer security. For applications that authenticate their own users, OAC ensures that original credentials reach the application unchanged, so existing sign-in flows keep working. CloudFront support for AWS Lambda Web Functions is available worldwide, except in the CloudFront China region. To get started, use the CloudFront Console, SDK, CLI, or CloudFormation to configure your Lambda Web Function as a CloudFront origin. For more information, refer to the CloudFront Developer Guide . There are no additional fees associated with this feature.

title: Amazon Connect Customer now prefills step-by-step guides for after contact work
product_change_reason: Post-contact forms automatically populate conversation data
announcement_text: Amazon Connect Customer can now fill in the step-by-step guides that agents complete after a contact, using information extracted from customer conversations, such as booking identifiers, claim numbers, and conversation summaries. Managers can set which information populates each form field. Agents can review and submit rather than manually typing in each field, saving time and improving data accuracy during after contact work. Contact center agents spend time after each contact entering frequently used information into a step-by-step guide. For example, an insurance agent who finishes a claims call might record the customer’s policy number, a summary of the call, and a disposition code. Now, managers can define rules for which information to extract from the conversation and which fields to automatically fill in the guide. The agent can then check the information, make any necessary corrections, and submit the guide, shortening after contact work and reducing data entry errors. You can use step-by-step guides with information extraction in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London). Contact summaries are also available in Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, see step-by-step guides in the Amazon Connect Customer administrator guide.

title: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports index-level encryption
product_change_reason: Search encryption keys configurable per index
announcement_text: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports index-level encryption, letting you encrypt each index at rest with its own AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. This helps you protect data with different ownership or sensitivity under separate keys on the same domain. For example, you can encrypt each tenant's data with its own key in a multi-tenant application. Index-level encryption builds on the existing encryption at rest capability in Amazon OpenSearch Service. To enable it, set the encryption mode to Native and specify a customer managed AWS KMS key when you create a new domain using the AWS Management Console or the AWS CLI. You can then register additional keys with the domain and use them to encrypt individual indexes. Index-level encryption is available for domains running OpenSearch version 3.3 or later in 14 AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London, Paris), and South America (São Paulo). There is no additional charge for the feature. Standard AWS KMS and OpenSearch Service charges apply. To get started, see Index-level encryption in the Amazon OpenSearch Service Developer Guide.

title: Amazon S3 Express One Zone is now available in 4 additional AWS Regions
announcement_text: The Amazon S3 Express One Zone storage class is now available in 4 additional AWS Regions: Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Jakarta), Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), and Africa (Cape Town). Amazon S3 Express One Zone is a high-performance, single-Availability Zone storage class purpose-built to deliver consistent single-digit millisecond data access for your most frequently accessed data and latency-sensitive applications. S3 Express One Zone delivers data access speed up to 10x faster and request costs up to 80% lower than S3 Standard. It enables workloads such as machine learning training, interactive analytics, and key-value caching in AI search engines to achieve fast data access with high durability and availability. With this expansion, S3 Express One Zone is now available in 19 AWS Regions . For pricing details, visit the S3 pricing page . To learn more, visit the product page and documentation .

title: AWS Secrets Manager adds managed external secrets support for Databricks and Twilio
product_change_reason: Managed secret rotation supports more SaaS providers
announcement_text: AWS Secrets Manager now extends its managed external secrets capability to include Databricks and Twilio, enabling you to automatically rotate the credentials that your data pipelines and messaging applications use to call these services. You set up rotation directly from the AWS Management Console or API without writing or maintaining any custom rotation Lambda functions. Long-lived credentials often stay unrotated because rotation is hard to set up and hard to distribute safely to the applications that use the updated credential. With managed external secrets, you can use Secrets Manager to rotate the Databricks personal access tokens that your jobs and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines use. You can also rotate the service principal OAuth client secrets that your automation workflows use. Each replacement personal access token retains the scopes of the token it replaces, so a narrowly scoped token stays narrowly scoped. For Twilio, you can use Secrets Manager to rotate the API keys and Auth Tokens that your applications use to send messages and place calls. For both services, you store the credential in Secrets Manager as a managed external secret and set a rotation schedule. Secrets Manager always returns the current credential, so your applications pick up rotated values automatically, with no code changes required. These integrations join existing managed external secrets support for BigID, Cisco Security Platform, Confluent Cloud, Datadog, GitLab, Jenkins, MongoDB Atlas, Netskope, Paddle, Salesforce, Snowflake, and SonarQube. Databricks and Twilio managed external secrets are available in all AWS Regions where AWS Secrets Manager managed external secrets is supported. To learn more, visit the AWS Secrets Manager managed external secrets documentation .

title: AWS Transfer Family supports custom ports for public SFTP servers
product_change_reason: Adds port and communication-mode controls to an existing SFTP server.
announcement_text: AWS Transfer Family now lets you configure custom ports on public SFTP servers and choose a communication mode for each port. You can support clients that require different ports or start SFTP connections differently on a single server. Previously, public SFTP servers accepted connections only on port 22 and used server-first communication. With this launch, you can configure up to three ports (22, or any port from 2000 to 65535), allowing you to use the port numbers your business or network requires and offer multiple ports on one server. Some SFTP clients initiate communication themselves, and their connections can occasionally stall on a server-first port. For each port, you can now select client-first or server-first communication and direct clients to the port that matches their connection behavior. Using a port other than 22 can also reduce unwanted connection attempts from automated scanners that target port 22. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where Transfer Family public SFTP servers are offered. To get started, visit the AWS Transfer Family console or use the AWS CLI or AWS SDKs. To learn more, visit Create an SFTP-enabled server in the AWS Transfer Family User Guide

title: Amazon RDS now supports the latest Cumulative Update for Microsoft SQL Server
announcement_text: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for SQL Server now supports the latest Cumulative Updates (CU) for Microsoft SQL Server. This release includes support for Microsoft SQL Server 2025 CU8 KB5104822 (RDS version 17.00.4075.5.v1). For additional information on the improvements and fixes included in these updates, see Microsoft documentation for KB5104822. We recommend that you upgrade your Amazon RDS for SQL Server instances to apply these updates using Amazon RDS Management Console, or by using the AWS SDK or CLI. You can learn more about upgrading your database instance in the Amazon RDS SQL Server User Guide for upgrading your RDS Microsoft SQL Server DB engine .

title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory now supports configurable time-to-live for long-term memory
announcement_text: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory now lets you set a time-to-live (TTL) on long-term memory records, so they are automatically deleted after a retention period you define. By default, long-term memory records do not expire. With this launch, you can configure a TTL to meet data-retention requirements, control storage growth, and ensure that stale insights age out of a memory over time. You can configure retention on the resource or specific records. Configuring or removing a TTL requires the new bedrock-agentcore:UpdateMemoryRecordExpirySpecification permission, giving you independent control over who can set record retention. To learn more, see Set a time-to-live for long-term memory records in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide. This feature is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory is supported.

title: Amazon DCV releases version 2026.0 with RHEL 10 support and new clients
product_change_reason: DCV supports additional platforms and clients
announcement_text: Amazon DCV 2026.0 is now available, adding support for RHEL 10, Rocky Linux 10, CentOS 10, and Ubuntu 26.04 along with a new macOS client and updated Windows and Linux clients. Amazon DCV is a high-performance remote display protocol that enables customers to securely access remote desktops and application sessions across Windows, Linux, and macOS. Amazon DCV 2026.0 includes the following key features and improvements: Support for RHEL 10, Rocky Linux 10, CentOS 10, and Ubuntu 26.04, with Linux hosts and sessions running on the modern Wayland display server A new macOS client with gamepad support, and updated Windows and Linux clients URL redirection on Windows hosts, so configured links opened in a remote session launch in the local browser on the client device Printer preferences redirection on Windows, giving remote sessions access to client-side printer settings Performance improvements, including H.264 frame slice support and slice-based multithreaded decoding on the Linux and macOS clients for lower latency Support for new macOS server versions on Amazon EC2 For more information about the new features and enhancements in Amazon DCV 2026.0, see the release notes or visit the Amazon DCV webpage to learn more and get started.

title: Amazon Location Service launches an interactive API Playground featuring Places, Routes and Maps APIs
announcement_text: Amazon Location Service now offers a complete, interactive API Playground that lets developers explore and test every Places, Routes, and Maps API visually without writing code. With this release, all 14 Amazon Location Service Places, Maps and Routes APIs are available in an interactive API Playground, where developers can make real API calls, see results rendered on an interactive map, adjust parameters, and copy ready-to-use request snippets directly into their applications. The API Playground covers Amazon Location Service's Places, Routes, and Maps APIs: search and geocoding (Geocode, ReverseGeocode, Autocomplete, Suggest, SearchText, SearchNearby, and GetPlace), route planning and optimization (CalculateRoutes, CalculateRouteMatrix, CalculateIsolines, OptimizeWaypoints, and SnapToRoads), and mapping (Dynamic Map and GetStaticMap). Customers can simulate validating delivery addresses, planning truck-safe multi-stop routes, visualizing drive-time service areas, or embedding maps into their apps — with no SDK setup or test scripts required. The API Playground is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (Ohio), US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Spain), Europe (Stockholm), and South America (São Paulo). To get started, visit the Amazon Location Service API Playground in the AWS Console, or learn more in the Developer Guide .

title: AWS Agent Registry now supports custom metadata for registry records
product_change_reason: Agent registry records accept custom metadata
announcement_text: AWS Agent Registry is the centralized, governed catalog for agents, MCP servers, agent skills, gateways, and custom resources within your organization. As organizations scale to hundreds of such resources, a name and description alone are insufficient for effective governance and discovery. Custom metadata lets you extend every registry record with your organization's own structured fields, so both people and automated systems can find and govern resources consistently. With custom metadata, publishers can record fields like team ownership, data classification, or review status directly on each registry record. You define a schema once per registry with common attributes, then extend it with type-specific fields — such as a model family for agent records. Each field supports free text, a URL, a Boolean, or a choice from a list of allowed values, and the registry validates required fields and values on every record creation or update. You can then filter search results on any custom metadata field from the AWS Management Console, the AWS CLI, the AWS SDKs, or the registry's MCP endpoint. Custom metadata is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Agent Registry is available: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Ireland). To learn more, visit the AWS Agent Registry documentation . For detailed setup guidance, see Define a custom metadata schema and Set custom metadata values on a record .

title: AWS Lambda durable functions increases durable operation and checkpoint payload limits
product_change_reason: Raises operation and checkpoint payload limits within existing durable execution.
announcement_text: Starting today, AWS Lambda durable functions increases the maximum number of durable operations per execution from 3,000 to 30,000, and the maximum checkpoint payload size from 256 KB to 1 MB. Higher operation limits let you safely do more work in a single execution including expanding iterative loops, polling for longer time periods, and building more complex rollback paths that run when a step fails. At 1 MB, checkpoint payloads match the maximum payload size of asynchronous Lambda invocations, and integration services such as Amazon SQS, and Amazon EventBridge, so a workflow can persist a full event from any of these sources in a single operation. AWS Lambda durable functions helps you build resilient multi-step applications and AI workflows that execute for up to one year, with built-in checkpointing, automatic retries, and waits that suspend execution without incurring compute charges. Every durable operation counts toward the per-execution limit, including each step attempt, each poll of a wait-for-condition, and each branch of a parallel or map operation. With 30,000 operations, a single execution has more room to coordinate complex, multi-step workflows, iterate across thousands of items, or poll an external system for weeks, without exceeding checkpoint limits. An agentic application can reason over thousands of model and tool calls, and with 1 MB checkpoints it persists larger conversation histories, model responses, and outputs from tools directly in the checkpoint instead of writing to external storage. For state larger than 1 MB, the JavaScript and Python SDKs include a FileSystem serializer that writes the payload to an Amazon EFS or Amazon S3 Files mount and checkpoints a pointer instead. The new limits apply in all AWS Regions where AWS Lambda durable functions is available. To learn more about these service limits, see the AWS Lambda developer guide .

title: Bring deep SageMaker AI expertise to your coding agent with the AWS AI/ML skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS
product_change_reason: SageMaker expertise packaged as coding-agent skill
announcement_text: Your coding agent can select, train, optimize and deploy models on Amazon SageMaker AI while working across the rest of your AWS environment in a single natural-language workflow. The AWS AI/ML skill is now a core skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS , so it works alongside the toolkit's other AWS skills like EC2, Bedrock, and more. We released the new AWS AI/ML skill on the Agent Toolkit for AWS. The toolkit is now the single, supported integration point, replacing the previous AWS Labs skills and plugins, with a consistent and easy install and update path. The skill is also pre-installed into SageMaker Studio JupyterLab for use with Kiro or your coding agent of choice. Moreover, we extended the SageMaker AI capability areas supported by skills. Inference optimization : optimize deployed models for latency, throughput, and cost Model customization : end-to-end guided fine-tuning workflows, from use case definition through training, evaluation and deployment Serverful training for both traditional ML and generative AI MLflow: experiment tracking and model lifecycle management JumpStart model deployment and model recommendations: deploy pre-built JumpStart models and get guided recommendations on the right model for the use case Processing jobs: data preparation and ETL on managed compute The AWS AI/ML skill is available at no additional charge; you pay only for the AWS resources your agents use. To get started, install the skill from the Agent Toolkit for AWS on GitHub, or use it pre-installed in SageMaker Studio JupyterLab. To learn more about using a coding assistant with your SageMaker AI workflows , see the Amazon SageMaker AI documentation.

title: AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now supports FSx for OpenZFS, NFS 4.2, and object metadata controls
product_change_reason: Adds transfer target protocol and metadata controls.
announcement_text: AWS DataSync Enhanced mode now supports Amazon FSx for OpenZFS as a source or destination location, NFS version 4.2 for on-premises NFS servers and FSx for OpenZFS file systems, and a new ObjectMetadata option for object storage transfers. Previously, customers transferring data to or from FSx for OpenZFS were limited to Basic mode. NFS 4.2 lets you transfer data from NFS servers on the latest version without reconfiguring them to an older protocol version. The ObjectMetadata option gives you control over whether an object's user metadata is copied to the destination, which helps when destination metadata must stay intact, such as buckets served by AWS Storage Gateway, or when source metadata keys are not compatible with the destination, such as Azure Blob Storage. Existing tasks remain unaffected and continue to run as scheduled. These capabilities are available for Enhanced mode tasks in all AWS Regions where AWS DataSync Enhanced mode is supported. To learn more, visit the AWS DataSync documentation .

title: AWS Deadline Cloud now helps users find their accessible resources in the Deadline Cloud monitor
product_change_reason: Render monitor discovers resources accessible to limited users
announcement_text: AWS Deadline Cloud now lets users who have access to specific queues, fleets, or jobs, rather than an entire farm, find the resources they can reach directly from the Deadline Cloud monitor. Deadline Cloud is a fully managed service that helps teams run compute-intensive workloads for visual effects, animation, product design, simulation, and gaming. Previously, a user with access to only one queue had to get the farm ID from an administrator before they could reach their work. With this launch, the Deadline Cloud monitor displays to users queues they have access to, the parent IDs needed to reach them, and their level of access, covering both direct and group-inherited permissions. Teams now can share a single monitor entry point (URL) across different permission levels without additional coordination. Resource discovery is available in all AWS Regions where Deadline Cloud is available. To learn more, visit the AWS Deadline Cloud user guide .

title: Amazon ECS adds LiveTaskCount and removes the charge for RunningTaskCount metric
product_change_reason: Adds live-task metric alongside pricing change.
announcement_text: Today, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) announces LiveTaskCount, a new ECS service metric that reports how many tasks are actively running in your service, available to all customers at no additional charge. Additionally, the existing RunningTaskCount metric in Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights no longer incurs a charge. LiveTaskCount reports the number of actively running ECS tasks across all desired states (ACTIVATING, RUNNING, and DEACTIVATING), including tasks still running while transitioning to a stopped state, for example, tasks undergoing connection draining during a scale-in event. This comprehensive state coverage makes LiveTaskCount well suited for autoscaling policies and capacity planning where a complete view of active, metric-generating tasks is required. It is available at no charge as part of ECS service utilization metrics and does not require opting in to CloudWatch Container Insights. The existing CloudWatch Container Insights RunningTaskCount metric tracks tasks where both the current and desired state are RUNNING, and continues to serve as a health and stability signal for customers who depend on it. With today's update, RunningTaskCount is now available at no additional charge for all CloudWatch Container Insights users. These updates are available in all AWS Regions where Amazon ECS is available. No action is required, and the pricing change for RunningTaskCount takes effect beginning October 1, 2026, and applies automatically. To learn more, see ECS CloudWatch metrics and ECS Container Insights metrics . For a pricing example, see Amazon CloudWatch pricing .

title: Amazon Route 53 now supports registrations, transfers, and renewals for Premium Domains
product_change_reason: Domain lifecycle operations support premium names
announcement_text: Amazon Route 53 Domains now supports Premium Domain Names. Customers can now search for, register, transfer, renew, and restore registry premium names directly through Route 53. Most domain registries set aside a selection of "premium" domains - names that are short, memorable, or in high demand. Previously, Route 53 Domains did not support these premium names, which meant customers who wanted them had to register and manage them through other registrars, fragmenting their portfolios across multiple providers. With this launch, customers can now discover and acquire premium domains directly in Route 53 Domains, consolidate their existing premium domains from other registrars, and manage premium and standard domains together through a single, unified experience. Finding and registering a premium domain works just like it does for standard domains. Premium domains appear automatically in domain search and availability results, with pricing shown upfront, so customers know the cost before they commit. To learn more about Amazon Route 53 Domains and start registering premium domains, visit the Amazon Route 53 Domains page . For a complete list of supported top-level domains, see the Route 53 TLD list .

title: Amazon S3 is now available on the Vercel Marketplace and v0 by Vercel
announcement_text: Amazon S3, including S3 Tables and S3 Vectors, is now available on the Vercel Marketplace and v0 by Vercel. Developers can create and connect S3 resources in seconds without leaving their development environment, getting the durability, scalability, and performance of S3 through Vercel's streamlined provisioning workflow. Millions of customers rely on S3 for low-cost, high-performance storage to power web and AI applications, but until now provisioning it from Vercel required navigating to the AWS Management Console. Now, S3 integrates directly into the Vercel developer experience, automatically handling resource provisioning and connection configuration. You can choose from S3 general purpose buckets for virtually any use case, S3 Tables for fully managed Apache Iceberg tables optimized for analytics workloads, or S3 Vectors to natively store and query vectors at scale. New AWS accounts created through Vercel include $100 in credits valid for up to six months, usable across Amazon S3, Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, and AWS Database services. Existing AWS customers can link their account to use S3 with their Vercel projects. Amazon S3 on Vercel is now available in all AWS Regions where Vercel is available. To get started, read the AWS News Blog , visit AWS on Vercel Marketplace , or launch v0 by Vercel .

title: AWS Backup now supports Amazon FSx file systems in the Asia Pacific (New Zealand) Region
announcement_text: AWS Backup now supports Amazon FSx for Lustre, Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, Amazon FSx for OpenZFS, and Amazon FSx for Windows File Server in the Asia Pacific (New Zealand) Region. With this launch, you can use AWS Backup to centrally automate and manage data protection for your Amazon FSx file systems in the Asia Pacific (New Zealand) Region, alongside your other supported AWS resources. You can create policy-based backup plans to schedule backups and apply retention rules, store backups in encrypted vaults, and restore file systems when needed. This helps you meet business continuity, disaster recovery, and regulatory compliance requirements from a single, centralized service. To get started, visit the AWS Backup console, AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), or AWS SDKs. For a complete list of supported Regions and features, visit the AWS Backup documentation . To learn more about AWS Backup, visit the product page and pricing page .

title: AWS HealthOmics expands container registry support for private workflows
product_change_reason: Omics workflow images support additional registries
announcement_text: You can now use container images from registries such as Seqera (Wave), NVIDIA NGC, and Google Artifact Registry with AWS HealthOmics expanded support for third-party container registries. You can use the containerized tools your workflows already rely on, without manually migrating images into Amazon ECR or editing your workflow definitions. AWS HealthOmics is a HIPAA-eligible service that helps healthcare and life sciences customers accelerate scientific breakthroughs at scale with fully managed bioinformatics workflows. With expanded container registry support, you can now instruct HealthOmics to copy container images, on your behalf, from newly supported registries into your Amazon ECR when running your private workflows. Previously, AWS HealthOmics could pull images only from registries supported through Amazon ECR pull-through cache (PTC). Your private workflows can now access Amazon ECR pull-through cache registries and the newly supported third party container registries, so you do not need to pull, re-push, or rewrite image URIs yourself. Expanded container registry support is now available in all AWS Regions where HealthOmics is available: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London), Israel (Tel Aviv), and Asia Pacific (Singapore, Seoul, Tokyo). To learn more, visit the third-party container image support documentation .

title: AWS HealthOmics introduces resource fallback order for Nextflow workflows
announcement_text: Today, AWS HealthOmics introduces the resource fallback directive for tasks in your Nextflow workflows, enabling you to define an ordered list of preferred accelerator types, including an option to fallback to CPU instances. Researchers and bioinformaticians can use this directive to reduce time spent diagnosing and resubmitting runs due to accelerator constraints and keep production workflows running. AWS HealthOmics is a HIPAA-eligible service that helps healthcare and life sciences customers accelerate scientific breakthroughs at scale with fully managed bioinformatics workflows. With resource fallback for Nextflow workflows, you can prioritize your preferred accelerator for your task. When your preferred accelerator is unavailable, HealthOmics automatically moves through your specified alternatives in the fallback without resubmission. Each accelerator profile has a configurable timeout, giving you control over how long HealthOmics searches for that accelerator before moving to the next. Shorter timeouts help you move quickly through the fallback order, while longer timeouts increase the probability of reserving your preferred accelerator. You can also include a CPU profile as a final fallback to increase the likelihood of your task reserving an instance. You can now use resource fallback for Nextflow workflows in all AWS HealthOmics Regions: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London), Israel (Tel Aviv), and Asia Pacific (Seoul, Singapore, Tokyo). To learn more, visit the advanced resource configuration and Nextflow specifics documentation.

title: AWS License Manager now supports license type conversions for Ubuntu Pro purchased through AWS Marketplace
announcement_text: AWS License Manager now supports in-place upgrades for EC2 Ubuntu LTS (Long Term Support) instances to Ubuntu Pro available on AWS Marketplace. This allows customers to strengthen their security posture and meet compliance requirements without rebuilding their fleet or migrating workloads to a new instance or AMI. With an Ubuntu Pro subscription, customers receive security patches for up to 10 years — extendable to 15 years with the Legacy add-on. This coverage extends beyond the base OS to thousands of additional packages, including widely used open-source applications such as NGINX, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Redis. Ubuntu Pro also supports Kernel Livepatch, which applies critical kernel security fixes without rebooting to minimize downtime. With this launch, customers, who have an existing Canonical Ubuntu Pro subscription through AWS Marketplace, can upgrade directly during the conversion workflow. Customers who do not yet have a subscription can subscribe to Canonical Ubuntu Pro from within the AWS License Manager console. The new feature is available in all commercial regions where AWS License Manager is available. To get started, navigate to the AWS License Manager console and the AWS License Manager User Guide .

title: Announcing Blockchain Snapshots on AWS for node bootstrapping
announcement_text: For blockchain node operators running Ethereum or Solana, AWS is announcing Blockchain Snapshots on AWS, an initiative that publishes pre-synced public blockchain node chain data in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) so you can bootstrap a node from a snapshot instead of peer-to-peer syncing from the network. These snapshots are hosted on Amazon S3 within AWS infrastructure, enabling customers running nodes on AWS benefit from reduced latency and optimized data transfer. Blockchain Snapshots on AWS republishes each network's authoritative snapshot in a format optimized for parallel extraction across multiple cores, reducing setup time, that an Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance can use. Snapshots cover Ethereum and Solana, are available at no charge, and refresh on the same cadence as the upstream provider. Use them to add capacity to a remote procedure call (RPC) fleet, recover a failed node, or re-sync a corrupted database. You can use Blockchain Snapshots on AWS in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), Europe (Ireland), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo). Access requires an Amazon EC2 instance in the same Region with an Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint. To get started, visit the Blockchain Snapshots on AWS documentation to access setup instructions and download the latest snapshots.

title: Amazon CloudWatch announces log routing and chained log parsers
product_change_reason: Adds conditional log routing and chained parser configuration.
announcement_text: Amazon CloudWatch now supports conditional log routing and chained parsers via pipelines, giving you more control over how log data is transformed and which CloudWatch log group it's sent to. CloudWatch pipelines is a fully managed service that ingests, transforms, and routes telemetry to CloudWatch without managing infrastructure. Log pipelines often carry a mix of event types that belong in different places, and individual events can nest one log format inside another. With conditional log routing, you define routes that send each event to a different CloudWatch log group based on conditions evaluated against processed fields, so you can separate events by severity, source, or type and apply the right retention and access controls to each. With chained parsers, you can apply multiple parser processors in sequence, where later parsers consume fields produced by earlier ones. For example, you can parse a JSON envelope first, then apply a Grok parser to a field it extracts. Together, these capabilities let you structure diverse log formats and route them to the right log groups in a single pipeline. Conditional routing and chained parsers are available in all commercial AWS Regions where CloudWatch pipelines is generally available. You can configure these capabilities using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. To get started, see the Amazon CloudWatch pipelines documentation .

title: AWS Lambda recursive loop detection now supports Amazon EventBridge Custom event buses
product_change_reason: Loop detection covers EventBridge custom buses
announcement_text: AWS Lambda recursive loop detection now automatically detects and stops recursive loops between Lambda Event Functions and Amazon EventBridge Custom event buses , helping protect you against unintended usage and unexpected charges from runaway workloads. Lambda recursive loop detection , enabled by default on your AWS account, automatically identifies when a Lambda Event Function is invoked recursively by a supported AWS service and stops the loop. You can use EventBridge Custom event buses to invoke Lambda Event Functions, building automation workflows and scheduling recurring tasks without managing any infrastructure. However, a misconfiguration or code defect can cause EventBridge rules to trigger your Event Functions recursively, resulting in runaway usage. Now, recursive loop detection supports EventBridge Custom buses, automatically stopping such loops and sending you an AWS Health Dashboard notification with troubleshooting instructions. EventBridge Custom event buses now support recursive loop detection in every commercial AWS Region where they are available. This feature is enabled by default on your account and requires no configuration. If your Event Function uses recursive loops intentionally, you can use the PutFunctionRecursionConfig API to turn off recursive loop detection for that function. To learn more about recursive loop detection, visit Lambda documentation .

title: Amazon RDS Proxy now supports SQL Server 2022
product_change_reason: RDS Proxy supports SQL Server engine
announcement_text: Amazon RDS Proxy , a fully managed, highly available database proxy for Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) , now supports Amazon RDS for SQL Server instances running major version 2022. Amazon RDS Proxy sits between your application and the database to pool and share established database connections, improving database efficiency and application scalability. For Amazon RDS for SQL Server Multi-AZ databases, RDS Proxy automatically connects to the standby database instance during a failure, preserves application connections, and helps reduce failover times by up to 83%. RDS Proxy supports standard IAM authentication for SQL Server, where your applications authenticate to the proxy using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) and RDS Proxy manages database connections using credentials stored in AWS Secrets Manager. You can enable Amazon RDS Proxy for your SQL Server 2022 database in a few steps on the Amazon RDS console, then connect by pointing your application to the RDS Proxy endpoint. To get started, see our documentation .

title: ARC Region switch adds four new capabilities
product_change_reason: Recovery orchestration adds automatic quota-parity checks and adjustment
announcement_text: Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) Region switch helps you orchestrate the failover of multi-Region applications to achieve a bounded recovery time during a Regional impairment. Today, Region switch adds four new capabilities: AWS Systems Manager Run Command execution block, payloads for custom action Lambda execution block, service quota parity checks, and wait for target group health feature for compute scaling actions. AWS Systems Manager Run Command execution block. During failover, you often need to run commands on managed instances and VMs. This execution block lets you invoke Run Command actions on managed instances during failover, with plan evaluation verifying that command documents target valid instances and that IAM permissions are correctly configured. Payloads for custom action Lambda execution block. ARC Region switch now lets you pass payloads to your custom action Lambda execution block, allowing reusability of your Lambda functions across recovery plans. Service quota checks. Service quota limits are a common failure mode during recovery. Region switch now verifies quota parity between your primary and standby Region, and automatically submits quota limit increases, reducing the risk of insufficient service quotas during recovery. Wait for target group health. Amazon ECS service scaling and Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group execution blocks help you provision compute capacity during recovery, but provisioned capacity may not be ready to serve traffic. The optional wait for target group health feature verifies that your provisioned capacity is ready to serve traffic. To get started, see the documentation for AWS Systems Manager Run Command execution block , custom action Lambda execution block , Service quota checks and the Wait for target group health for Amazon ECS service scaling execution block and Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group execution block .

title: AWS Security Hub now supports resource criticality for prioritization
announcement_text: Today, AWS Security Hub adds resource criticality to exposure prioritization, helping central security teams focus on the exposures that threaten their most business-critical resources. You can set criticality with an automation rule, for example marking every compute resource in a specific account as Very High. The rule applies to resources already in your inventory and to new resources as Security Hub discovers them. Security Hub also infers criticality from resource tags and resource names, with no configuration required, and records which source determined the value. Criticality appears as a column on the Resources page for sorting, filtering, and grouping, and on the Impact assessment tab of an exposure finding. Resource criticality is included with Security Hub Essentials at no additional cost and is always on for all customers. Resource criticality is included with Security Hub Essentials at no additional cost and requires no new enablement. To learn more, see AWS Security Hub User Guide and the AWS Security Hub product page . For a list of AWS Regions where Security Hub is available, see the AWS Region table .

title: AWS Transfer Family now supports AWS Secrets Manager storage for SFTP server host keys
product_change_reason: SFTP host keys stored in customer Secrets Manager
announcement_text: AWS Transfer Family now lets you store SFTP server host keys in AWS Secrets Manager in your own AWS account. This gives you greater control over your server identity and helps simplify server migrations and failover. Previously, Transfer Family stored host keys within the service, so you could not retrieve the associated private key material. With this launch, you can choose Secrets Manager as the storage type when creating a server or importing a host key. You can then retrieve the private key material and reuse the same host key across servers and AWS Regions. For example, you can use it on a standby server for failover or on a replacement server during migration, without requiring clients to trust a new host key. AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies let you control who can retrieve the stored keys. You can also migrate existing host keys to Secrets Manager, which may require additional steps; see the AWS Transfer Family User Guide for details. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transfer Family is available. To learn more, see Store SFTP server host keys in AWS Secrets Manager in the AWS Transfer Family User Guide. To get started, go to the AWS Transfer Family console .

title: AWS Transfer Family console supports SVG logos and ICO favicons for web apps
product_change_reason: Adds SVG and ICO branding asset compatibility.
announcement_text: The AWS Transfer Family console now supports SVG files for logos and ICO files for favicons in web apps, with upload limits increased to 2 MB. This gives you more flexibility to use existing branding assets when customizing your web app. Previously, the console accepted only JPG and PNG files and limited logo uploads to 50 KB and favicon uploads to 20 KB. The console automatically resizes images and converts them to JPG or PNG before saving them. Existing API upload limits and format requirements remain unchanged. These capabilities are available in all AWS Regions where Transfer Family web apps are offered. To learn more, see the Transfer Family web apps tutorial .

title: Muse Spark Open model now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
product_change_reason: JumpStart model catalog adds Muse Spark
announcement_text: Meta's Muse Spark Open is now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, expanding the portfolio of foundation models available to AWS customers. This coding-optimized open-weight model from Meta is purpose-built for agentic coding workflows, bringing multi-step reasoning and tool calling to enterprise software engineering on AWS infrastructure. Muse Spark Open is designed for long-running coding agents and multimodal engineering workflows. Built on a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture with 816B total parameters and 42B active per token, it delivers the capacity of a very large network while keeping per-token compute closer to that of a much smaller dense model. The model holds a 1M-token context window, enabling it to ingest an entire project—including dependencies, legacy code, and thousands of files—without splitting tasks into smaller pieces. It accepts text, images, documents, audio, and audio-video as input and generates text output. Trained on real developer workflows such as multi-file refactors and long debugging sessions, it plans, acts, observes results, and self-corrects over long horizons rather than making single tool calls. SageMaker JumpStart offers two variants: BF16 (Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B) and NVFP4 quantized (Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4), with the NVFP4 variant requiring roughly a quarter of the memory for cost-efficient deployment. With SageMaker JumpStart, customers can deploy Muse Spark Open with just a few clicks, with the endpoint running in their own AWS account for full control over source code and prompts. To get started with this model, navigate to the SageMaker JumpStart model catalog in the SageMaker console or use the SageMaker Python SDK to deploy the model to your AWS account. For more information about deploying and using foundation models in SageMaker JumpStart, see the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart documentation .

title: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore expands to AWS GovCloud and 3 Regions
announcement_text: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now available in four additional AWS Regions: US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Sydney), and AWS GovCloud (US-West). Web Search is a fully managed tool that provides AI agents with current grounding from the web, enabling more accurate and up-to-date responses for tasks such as research, summarization, and question answering. With this expansion, customers can build agents that retrieve web information closer to their applications and end users with lower latency. Customers with government workloads can now use Web Search in the AWS GovCloud (US-West) Region to meet compliance and data residency requirements. To learn more about Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, see the Web Search tool documentation . To learn about pricing, visit Amazon Bedrock AgentCore pricing . For Region availability, visit Supported AWS Regions .

title: Amazon DynamoDB Streams now supports timestamp-based stream processing
product_change_reason: Stream readers can select timestamp starting position
announcement_text: Amazon DynamoDB Streams now supports timestamp-based stream processing, enabling you to begin reading stream records from a specific point in time. Previously, you could only start from the oldest retained record (up to 24 hours old) or from new records written after you start consuming the stream. Now, you can supply a timestamp and begin processing at the first record written at or after that time using the AT_TIMESTAMP shard iterator type. Timestamp-based stream processing can be used with the Amazon Kinesis Client Library (KCL) through the DynamoDB Streams Kinesis adapter. It helps you avoid reprocessing entire retained streams or missing records when resuming stream consumption, supporting common use cases such as recovery after an interruption, data replay for debugging and auditing by reading from a specific point in the past, skipping a backlog by resuming from a recent timestamp near the latest records, and synchronizing after a restore by beginning at the export timestamp following a point-in-time recovery (PITR) export. Timestamp-based stream processing is available in all commercial AWS Regions, the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, and the China Regions. There is no additional charge for this feature beyond standard GetRecords API request charges. To get started, see Amazon DynamoDB Streams timestamp documentation in the DynamoDB developer guide.

title: Amazon MSK Connect and AWS Glue Schema Registry are now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) region
product_change_reason: Expands Kafka integrations to Sovereign Cloud.
announcement_text: Starting today, Amazon MSK Connect and the AWS Glue Schema Registry are available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) region. Together with Amazon MSK Standard brokers, already available in the region, these launches give customers running streaming workloads on the AWS European Sovereign Cloud a more complete set of tools to build, connect, and govern their Apache Kafka applications. MSK Connect lets you run fully managed Kafka Connect clusters with Amazon MSK - deploy, monitor, and scale connectors that move data between Apache Kafka and external systems like databases, file systems, and search indices, with no infrastructure to provision, automatic scaling, and pay-as-you-go pricing. Complementing it, the AWS Glue Schema Registry - a serverless, free feature of AWS Glue - lets you validate and control the evolution of streaming data using Apache Avro, JSON, and Protobuf schemas. Acting as a centralized repository for data format and structure across decoupled applications, it reduces data validation logic, cross-team coordination, and downstream failures, and integrates with C# and Java applications built for Amazon MSK , Amazon Kinesis Data Streams , Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink , and AWS Lambda . To get started, visit the Amazon MSK Developer Guide and the AWS Glue Schema Registry documentation.

title: Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow now offers AI agent skills
product_change_reason: Airflow operations expertise packaged as agent skills
announcement_text: Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (MWAA) now integrates with the Agent Toolkit for AWS to provide built-in AI agent skills that let you author, debug, and test MWAA workflows and upgrade MWAA environments using any AI coding assistant that supports agent skills. The four skills are authoring-mwaa-workflow, debugging-mwaa-workflow, testing-mwaa-workflow, and upgrading-mwaa-environments. Together they let your AI assistant interact directly with MWAA using natural language, reducing the manual effort of building and maintaining data pipelines. For example, you can describe an ETL pipeline in plain language and the authoring skill generates a working DAG complete with task dependencies and error handling. The Amazon MWAA AI agent skills work with both Amazon MWAA Provisioned and Amazon MWAA Serverless environments, and are available in all AWS Regions where Amazon MWAA is available. To get started, install the aws-data-analytics plugin and configure your AI coding assistant to use the MWAA agent skills. To learn more, see Using agent skills with Amazon MWAA in the Amazon MWAA User Guide and the Agent Toolkit for AWS documentation .

title: Amazon S3 Metadata now available in six additional AWS Regions
announcement_text: Amazon S3 Metadata is now available in six additional AWS Regions: Asia Pacific (Hyderabad), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (New Zealand), Asia Pacific (Taipei), Asia Pacific (Thailand), and Mexico (Central). S3 Metadata is a fast and easy way to instantly discover and understand your S3 data with automated, easily queried metadata that updates in near real time. This helps you curate, identify, and use your S3 data for business analytics, real-time inference applications, and more. S3 Metadata automatically populates metadata for both new and existing objects, providing you with a comprehensive, queryable view of your data. Annotations extend S3 Metadata, letting you attach rich business context directly to your objects in JSON, XML, or YAML, with up to 1 GB per object. To query annotations at scale, you can surface them in S3 Metadata annotation tables in these Regions. With this launch, S3 Metadata is now generally available in 38 AWS Regions . For pricing details, visit the S3 pricing page . To learn more, visit the product page and documentation .

title: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus Collector now available in Asia Pacific (New Zealand) Region
announcement_text: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus collector, a fully-managed agentless collector for Prometheus metrics, is now available in Asia Pacific (New Zealand). Customers in New Zealand can now run their Prometheus-compatible monitoring workloads in-region, with lower latency for local workloads and the ability to keep their data in-country. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus collector discovers and collects Prometheus metrics from your container workloads without the need to run and operate collection agents yourself.
